reviews.comment: Dr. Karpetis does not foster a healthy learning environment well at all. On day 1 of class, he told us that we would all fail the class. Lectures were hard to follow and feedback was hardly given. The homework grades were completion, and the rest of the grade was determined by 3 exams. We were not given exam 1 grades back until after we took exam 2
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Karpetis is a mid professor that uses intimidation as a form of teaching. Asking questions in class will always lead to him making fun of you even if it's totally unnecessary and the questions are good. Gave the midterm grade the last week of class and the final was extremely hard and unexpected based on homework and the midterm difficulty.

Dr. Karpetis is intense and can be intimidating, but he really does care. If you show him that you are trying to learn in his class, he will pass you (even if numerically, you are failing). His lectures can be confusing and a bit draining, but definitely don't skip his classes. Take notes, read the textbook, and do the homework.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Karpetis is by far my favorite prof at tamu. You go to class kinda expecting to get yelled at, but by the end of the semester, you've learned more than you thought it was possible to learn in a semester. It's pretty hard to prepare for exams, but he curves quite well at the end.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Karpetis is an interesting professor, very memeable, always talking about how this isn't high school and how we need to hit the books, but he has a point. Read the textbook and do the hw instead of chegging it. Ask questions, even though he seems scary, he cares. Most importantly, PUT IN EFFORT. If you work hard and show it, you'll get an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Karpetis is one of my favorite professors. Do the reading, participate in class, and ask questions. He can be harsh at times, but he loves when students are invested in the class and in aerospace. The class is hard, but if you apply yourself and put on a thick skin he'll teach you how to think and be an engineer, not just the subject matter.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: While he is not the nicest man on the face of the Earth, whenever he gets upset with the class, he does have a legitimate reason. AERO 212 really isn't as hard as everyone makes it out to be in you READ THE TEXTBOOK. With that said, the man is a genius and likes teaching when students ask questions and come prepared to class.

Adonis is a man on a whole other level. His Tests are 4 questions long and they will destroy you. YOU NEED TO READ THE BOOK. I made the mistake of not reading the first weeks. always try to read them before the lectures. DONT FORGET TO HIT THE BOOKS!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough
